That is attractive on the arithmetic, and the downside cases in Figure 50 show the fair trough is bounded.

The dashboard rates total shareholder return and valuation F, and the disagreement with this memo is about timing. The dashboard gives an F because its rating and the memo's re-based modal return differ by two grades or more. The disagreement is between a Bottoming-phase guideline multiple that prices in the resolution of CVS's two worries and a current multiple that does not. This memo's view is that the dashboard's rating is right about the next six months and the guideline is right about the following twelve.

Against the market. The sell-side's median target of 1,600p implies about +22 percent and relies on the same mechanism: a re-rating to about 15x on flat-to-slightly-lower estimates. We agree on the mechanism and the destination. We are more explicit that nothing in the next six months supplies the trigger, and that the earnings leg alone is worth about 10 percent a year.

Conclusion: the model returns +38 percent to December 2027 at the guideline multiple, of which about 10 points is earnings we can defend and about 25 points is a multiple that needs a named chief executive and an organic print of 3 percent or more; the probability-weighted return is therefore nearer +25 percent, with a floor of about +10 to +17 percent if the numbers are delivered and nothing else happens.

Score: 79, set by the Rater. About +25% sits in the B band near 80 on the scale, and the three-year +65% supports it, but the near term is tilted down with a disappointing appointment giving about nil and a fair trough at -13% to -19%, so I hold it just below the scale point for the skew.

#13 Summary conclusion

CVS is a disciplined roll-up compounding adjusted EPS at 9 to 11 percent a year on a stalled UK organic core. It trades at 11.6x to 12.4x two-year-forward earnings and about 7x EBITDA, against private-market prices of 9x to 14x EBITDA. Its regulatory tail has gone, its labour constraint has eased, an activist is on the register, and its chief executive's successor has not been named.

CVS's earnings are predictable because the growth is transacted: the lower share count, the acquisitions already owned and the easier comparatives. FY2027 EPS should be 93p to 94p, within a range of 82p to 104p, with a 60 percent chance of landing within ±5 percent of the base.

CVS's share price is not predictable, because 87 percent of its movement comes from CVS's own news, and the news for the next six months is three prints that will look softer than the business (group LFL growth about 1.5 percent; flat-to-down margins on the R&D release) plus an undated appointment.

Guidance and estimates hold no cushion of conservatism to unlock. The favourable gaps are slower to arrive: the share count, out-year acquisitions, a buyback renewal, and options on the laboratories and a take-private.

The modelled return of +38 percent to December 2027 is two-thirds multiple, and the multiple needs two company events: a credible chief executive and an H2 FY2027 organic print of 3 percent or more.

The practical conclusion for Richard: the fundamentals are not unusually skewed to the positive today. They are likely to become so between March and September 2027, after the soft prints, with the comparatives easy, the acquisitions annualised, the chief executive named and the out-year arithmetic visible, unless the appointment arrives first and pulls the window forward. The downside is bounded (about −13 to −19 percent to a fair trough) and cushioned by a private-market value well above the price.

What to watch. Four lines carry the forecast: the share count, acquisitions completed, the clinical staff ratio and the R&D credit recognised. Three levels raise the alarm: Healthy Pet Club members (500,000), the Advanced tier count (25,000) and practice LFL growth against 1.0 percent.

The four aggregate scores

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 48, set by the Rater. The funded capital-allocation forces (topic 2) turn EPS from decline to about 10% a year (topic 6, bottom of B), but the external picture is a modest headwind (topic 1), pricing power and operating leverage are dormant (topic 5) and the change that would most alter the operating trajectory is a vacancy, so the net change is close to neutral and just negative; I weigh the funded mechanics more than the memo's 35.
Foundations' Robustness: 43, set by the Rater. A rational, defensive industry structure is offset by ordinary advantages, a weak economic profile (ROIC 3.1%, an R&D credit inside the margin, low returns on recent deals) and management that has not grown per-share value (topic 3 at 45), and the record of meeting only cut numbers and missing organic targets for three years (topic 4 at 40) takes it a little lower.
Setups' Fit/Crispness: 37, set by the Rater. The memo finds the case a hybrid of a cleared-concern recovery whose worry has been replaced by a flat organic engine and an empty chair, and a mechanical serial-acquirer EPS story that tracks rather than upgrades consensus, and it calls neither setup crisp, so the fit is clearly below typical.
Case Riskiness: 55, set by the Rater. Few trackable drivers, transacted growth and a narrow earnings cone make the earnings lower-risk than most (topic 9 at 57), but the binary leadership and R&D-credit tails and the stock's history of sharp de-ratings keep the share-price risk high, leaving it a little better than typical.

Appendix: a comment from the Financial Analyst on reporting basis

Our model keeps one reporting basis for history and forecasts. The checks below suggest that consensus may use a different basis for some lines, so part of the gap between our forecasts and consensus on those lines may not be a difference of view. Nothing has been adjusted in the model.

What the checks found:

  • FY2026 earnings per share: 0.86 on the brokers' basis against 0.56 on our model's basis (+53.9%).

Facts in the data file that commonly explain such a gap:

  • Amortisation of acquired intangibles over the last twelve months: -26.0 before tax (-0.38 per share); our model's FY2026 history does not exclude it (its EBITA equals EBIT). Brokers' adjusted figures often exclude it.
  • Hybrid bond coupons and capitalised leases are not in the data file; check the company's reporting where relevant.

How to read this page

Every rating of this stock on one page: the Rater's 1-100 number, its letter and the Rater's own reason (at most three sentences, taken from the ratings file; nothing newly written). The number is the company's approximate standing in the Universe of about 1,300 listed European companies (90 = better than about 9 in 10; 50 = typical). A letter follows its item's rule: rank among the stocks scored (A the top 10%; B+ and B the next 15%; C+, C and C- the next 25%; D the next 25%; F the bottom 25%); or Richard's cut-offs on the measure for the four numerical topics (forecast financials, current momentum, the fair multiple, total shareholder return). On the change-forces items the number carries a sign (50 = neither positive nor negative) and the letter is the rank, so read the two together. "9th of 30 stocks scored" is the stock's place on that item. A dashed badge is provisional (fewer than 30 stocks scored).
